questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

In order to win the competition, one has to be __creative__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **more creative**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The use of a **comparative degree** is appropriate here.
 
• In the sentence it is written that a person can win a competition only if he/she is better or more creative than others. 
 
 
• ***Example:** One has to be faster in order to win a race.*
 
 

Hence, **more creative** should substitute **creative** in the given sentence. 

 
• The correct answer is **option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• To describe, quantify, modify or identify nouns/pronouns, adjectives are used or reused. Adjectives have their own degrees called **degrees of adjectives** or degrees of comparison that compare one thing/person to another. 
 
• There are** three degree**s of comparison: **Positive, Comparative, and Superlative**. 
 
• Example:
 
 
• Riya is beautiful. (Positive degree)
 
• Riya is more beautiful than Diya. (Comparative degree)
 
• Riya is the most beautiful girl in our class. (Superlative degree)

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

The new bride is going to be admired by everyone in the family.

options.text: Everybody in the family is going to admire the new bride.
Everybody in the family was admiring the new bride.
Everybody in the family has been going to admire the new bride.
Everybody in the family was going to admire the new bride.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Everybody in the family is going to admire the new bride.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in **Future (going to)** tense.
 
• The structure of this tense in active and passive forms is as follows:
 
 
• **Active voice:** Subject + is/am/are going to + V1 + Object.
 
• **Passive voice:** Object + is/am/are going to + be + V3 + by + Subject.
 
 
 
• **Example**:
 
 
• **Active voice: **I am going to do that work.
 
• **Passive voice:** That work is going to be done by me.
 
 

Hence, the correct option is **Option 1**.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

Admittance was refused to him by the airport security.

options.text: The airport security is refusing him admittance.
The airport security has refused him admittance.
The airport security had refused him admittance .
The airport security refused him admittance.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **The airport security refused him admittance**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in **Simple Past **tense.
 
• The structure of active and passive forms in Simple Past tense is as follows:
 
 
• **Active:** Subject + V2 + Object
 
• **Passive**: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• **Active**: Our teacher taught this chapter in the last class.
 
• **Passive**: This chapter was taught by our teacher in the last class. 
 
 

Hence, the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice is **The airport security refused him admittance.**

__
 
• **Expended: **spent or used money, time, care, etc. in doing something.
 
• **Exhausted: **depleted of energy, force, or strength.

• Thus, the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word is **exhausted**.

Thus, the correct answer is **option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Earned: The verb "earned" refers to having received something in return for labor or services, it can also be used to suggest that something was deserved because of actions or qualities.
 
 
• **Example:** "She earned a good salary from her job."
 
 
 
• Enjoyed: The verb "enjoyed" means to have derived pleasure from something or to have a pleasant or satisfying experience.
 
 
• **Example: **"We really enjoyed our vacation in Hawaii." 
 
 
 
• Encashed: The verb "encashed" means to convert a check or other financial instrument into cash; it is often used in contexts like encashing a check or bond.
 
 
• **Example: **"I encashed my paycheck at the bank." e.g., "He encashed his savings bonds when he needed the money."
